knowledge:
- key_parameters: se=A SummarizedExperiment object containing protein intensities and metadata ;; thr=The threshold for the number of missing values allowed per protein in filter_missval ;; fun=The imputation method used in impute, such as "man", "bpca", "knn", "QRILC", "MLE", or "MinProb" ;; type=The type of contrast to test in test_diff, such as "control", "all", or "manual" ;; alpha=The significance threshold (FDR) in add_rejections ;; lfc=The log2 fold change threshold in add_rejections
- alternatives: limma=for general linear modeling of expression data without proteomics-specific imputation workflows ;; MSstats=for complex mass spectrometry experimental designs and peptide-level processing
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing label-free or isobaric-labeled mass spectrometry proteomics data to identify differentially expressed or enriched proteins, particularly when systematic handling of missing values is required.
- pitfalls: Imputing missing values before filtering out proteins with excessive missing data can introduce severe artifacts and false positives ;; Choosing an inappropriate imputation method (e.g., assuming missing-at-random for missing-not-at-random data) can bias the differential analysis.

workflows.name: differential_protein_expression
workflows.intent: Identify differentially expressed proteins from mass spectrometry intensity data using a robust filtering, normalization, imputation, and linear modeling workflow.
input: proteinGroups.txt (tabular file containing protein IDs, gene names, and intensity columns from MaxQuant or similar)
experimental_design.txt (tabular file mapping sample names to experimental conditions and replicate numbers)
workflows.stages: 1. Generate unique names for proteins using make_unique ;; 2. Create a SummarizedExperiment object using make_se ;; 3. Filter out proteins with too many missing values using filter_missval ;; 4. Normalize the data using normalize_vsn ;; 5. Impute missing values using impute ;; 6. Test for differential expression using test_diff ;; 7. Define significant proteins using add_rejections ;; 8. Extract results table using get_results
workflows.code:
data_unique <- make_unique(proteins_tbl, "Gene.names", "Protein.IDs", delim = ";")
se <- make_se(data_unique, columns, experimental_design)
filt <- filter_missval(se, thr = 0)
norm <- normalize_vsn(filt)
imputed <- impute(norm, fun = "MinProb")
diff <- test_diff(imputed, type = "control", control = "Ctrl")
dep <- add_rejections(diff, alpha = 0.05, lfc = 1)
results <- get_results(dep)
